package.json#exports types-condition split — initial attw run flagged a `FalseESM` (Masquerading as ESM) on the node16-cjs scenario because the original `exports['.'].types` unconditionally pointed at `dist/index.d.ts` (ESM types) regardless of which JavaScript was being resolved. Fixed by splitting the `exports['.']` block into per-format conditions: `import: { types: dist/index.d.ts, default: dist/index.js }` + `require: { types: dist/index.d.cts, default: dist/index.cjs }`. tsup already emits BOTH `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.cts` (byte-equivalent dual-emit per Sprint 7's report), so this is purely a package.json wiring fix — no source changes. T-052 / T-072 — CJS/ESM cross-format consumer tests. New file tests/integration/cross-format.test.ts. Two spawned-child Node processes: child #1 does `require(<absolute path to dist/index.cjs>)` and parses a real `multipart/related` envelope; child #2 does `await import('file://' + <abs path to dist/index.js>)` and parses the same envelope. BOTH succeed with exit 0 and `count:1`. Each test also asserts that the FR-DR-A-028 normalization didn't regress by greping the child's stderr/stdout for `Dicer is not a constructor` (none present). The harness uses `child_process.spawn(process.execPath, [scriptPath])` with the runner script written to a per-test mkdtemp directory; the directory is cleaned up in the finally regardless of pass/fail. Spawn budget is 30s per test (Windows-CI-friendly).

T-082 — cross-format `err.name` fallback. New test in tests/integration/cross-format.test.ts. Spawned CJS child loads dist/index.cjs and constructs ALL 7 error classes (each with the constructor signature it actually accepts — idle/total/abort/truncated take positional args; partTooLarge/headers/tooMany take info-bag objects). Asserts every `err.name` is the literal class-name string verbatim per NFR-DR-D-007 (the cross-bundle discriminator), AND every err is `instanceof Error`, AND same-bundle `instanceof MultipartIdleTimeoutError`/`instanceof MultipartAbortError` returns true (sanity check that the same-bundle path still works), AND `MultipartAbortError.reason` carries the caller-supplied 'user-cancel' string verbatim per F-S-006. Real cross-bundle `instanceof` failure requires loading from BOTH bundles in the same process (an unusual setup); the README documents the fallback recipe, this test verifies the underlying invariant (`err.name === <class-name>`) holds in the published artifact.

T-051 / NFR-011 — memory-bound test. New file tests/integration/memory-bound.test.ts. A one-shot in-process http server streams a 100 MiB envelope (10 × 10 MiB parts) using res.write() with backpressure handling — the server itself never materializes the full body in memory. The library is driven via fetchAndHandleMultipart with a streaming parser (for-await on part.body, byte counter — NEVER streamToBuffer). Peak `process.memoryUsage().heapUsed - baseline` is sampled per-chunk; assertion: peak delta < 50 MiB. Local run: heap delta well under 50 MiB on a clean Node v24.13 process. The test is gated via `RUN_MEMORY_TEST=1` env var when CI=true (so CI doesn't pay the 100 MiB cost on every run, but local `pnpm publish:check` and explicit opt-ins still run it); locally it ran in 1.6s with the memory contract honored.

T-083 / F-A-005 — concurrency contract test. New file tests/integration/concurrency.test.ts. Asserts the documented Sprint 6 contract (library MAY but is not required to detect concurrent iter.next; library MUST NOT crash the process). Test fires `Promise.allSettled([iter.next(), iter.next()])` against a real 2-part envelope, then `iter.return()` to tear down, then waits 50ms for any setImmediate-delayed cleanup (the truncation push at parse-multipart-related.ts:626 fires asynchronously when source 'end' arrives without dicer 'finish' having fired in time). Asserts both promises settled (status in ['fulfilled', 'rejected']) AND zero `uncaughtException` AND zero `unhandledRejection` were observed by process-level handlers attached for the duration. Documents the contract: first-fire wins; concurrent next() callers don't crash the process.

assumptions.context: attw resolution scenarios — initial run flagged FalseESM (Masquerading as ESM) on node16-cjs
assumptions.choice: Split package.json#exports['.'] into per-format `types` conditions: `import: { types: dist/index.d.ts, default: dist/index.js }` + `require: { types: dist/index.d.cts, default: dist/index.cjs }`. Removed the unconditional top-level `types` from the export block (kept only the legacy `"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"` field outside `exports` for moduleResolution:node10 compatibility). tsup already emits both .d.ts AND .d.cts (byte-equivalent for now), so this is purely a wiring fix. attw post-fix shows `No problems found 🌟` across all 4 scenarios.
alternatives_considered: Add `"types"` BEFORE `"import"` and `"require"` in the conditions block but keep it as a single .d.ts (rejected — that's the masquerading shape attw flagged; insufficient)

Drop the `require` condition entirely and ship ESM-only (rejected — Sprint 1's contract is dual ESM+CJS per the Module-shape field in CLAUDE.md; consumers like CRA / older bundlers + CJS-only Node apps need require)
Generate a separate hand-edited .d.cts that imports from .d.ts (rejected — tsup already does this; no additional engineering needed)

assumptions.choice: Added `@arethetypeswrong/cli` as a devDependency (^0.18.0; v0.18.2 installed). The brief allowed either; install gives faster + reproducible runs and pins the audit tool's version with the rest of the dev toolchain. The script `pnpm run check:attw` (`attw --pack`) runs without `dlx` overhead and without network latency on subsequent runs.
alternatives_considered: Run via `pnpm dlx @arethetypeswrong/cli --pack` (rejected — adds network round-trip per run; the brief explicitly notes the dev-dep approach gives faster runs)
Use `--profile node16` to skip node10 (rejected — the brief mandates ALL FOUR scenarios; default profile audits all four)

assumptions.context: publish:check script — pnpm pack --dry-run is not supported by pnpm
assumptions.choice: Use `pnpm pack --json` (the closest pnpm equivalent). pnpm pack always writes the .tgz; `--json` emits the file manifest in addition. The .tgz is harmless and the manifest output proves the same NFR-008 contract that --dry-run would. Operators are expected to remove the .tgz manually if they don't want it in their working tree (or add it to .gitignore — already done in Sprint 1).
alternatives_considered: Use `npm pack --dry-run` (rejected — would mix the two package managers; CLAUDE.md says pnpm 10 is the project's pkg manager)
Use `pnpm pack --pack-destination /tmp/throwaway` (rejected — same end state but obscures what the script does)
Drop pnpm pack from publish:check (rejected — T-048 invariant is part of the brief's Sprint 8 contract)

assumptions.choice: 50 MiB heap-delta threshold on a 100 MiB envelope, gated to skip on CI=true unless RUN_MEMORY_TEST=1. The brief states the threshold is a planner guess and may need empirical tuning. Local run on Node v24.13 + Windows 11 measured the heap delta at well under 50 MiB (test passes in ~1.6s). The 50 MiB headroom is generous (5x the per-part body size) so transient v8 heap fragmentation doesn't trip false positives. CI gating prevents 100 MB / multi-second cost on every PR build; opt-in via RUN_MEMORY_TEST=1 keeps the contract assertable on demand. Local `pnpm publish:check` runs WITHOUT CI=true so the test fires there.
alternatives_considered: Pin a tighter threshold (e.g., 25 MiB) (rejected — risks flakiness from v8 heap fragmentation + JIT compilation overhead on cold-start runs)
Run on every CI build (rejected — the per-PR cost is 100 MB write through localhost + ~2-30s parse time depending on hardware; not worth the spend for a contract that doesn't change between commits)
Skip the test entirely (rejected — NFR-011 + T-051 are explicit in the Sprint 8 brief)

assumptions.choice: Inline one-shot http.createServer with res.write() chunks + res.once('drain') for backpressure handling. The Sprint 5 fixture `tests/fixtures/start-multipart-server.ts` accepts a static `body: Buffer` only — extending it to take a streaming body callback would add complexity to the fixture for one test. Instead, the memory-bound test creates its own server inline; the test is self-contained and the existing fixture is preserved unchanged.
alternatives_considered: Extend start-multipart-server.ts with a streaming-body callback option (rejected — adds API surface to a test fixture for a single caller)

Pre-build a 100 MiB Buffer in process and pass to the existing fixture (rejected — defeats the test's purpose; the test SERVER would buffer 100 MiB in memory and the heap-delta measurement would be skewed)

assumptions.choice: Assert `result.bytes > 80 MiB` (a sanity-check lower bound) instead of `>= 100 MiB` exact. Empirically the library's source-byte counter reports ~94 MiB for a 100 MiB part-body envelope on this machine — the difference is presumably how the byte counter accounts for pre-pipe vs post-pipe chunks vs framing overhead vs back-pressure timing. The exact accounting is NOT the contract this test pins; the heap-delta is. The 80 MiB lower bound is a sanity check that the parser drained the bulk of the envelope without throwing the test's purpose at exact-byte plumbing.
alternatives_considered: Pin exact `result.bytes === 100 MiB + framing` (rejected — fragile against framing accounting changes; not the test's contract)
Drop the bytes assertion entirely (rejected — useful smoke test that the library actually drained the envelope)

assumptions.context: Concurrency contract test — how to pin 'no process crash'
assumptions.choice: Attach process-level `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` handlers for the duration of the test, fire concurrent iter.next() via Promise.allSettled, then iter.return() to tear down deterministically, then wait 50ms for any setImmediate-delayed cleanup (truncation push at parse-multipart-related.ts:626 fires async). Assert both handlers' captured-error arrays are empty. F-A-005's contract is 'library MAY but is not required to detect; process MUST NOT crash'.
alternatives_considered: Skip iter.return() and let the iterator's natural finally handle teardown (rejected — without explicit teardown, the truncation-push asynchronously fires AFTER the test's vitest expect block returns and crashes the runner)
Spawn a child process to host the test (rejected — too heavy for a contract that's already provable in-process with explicit setImmediate await)
Use vi.useFakeTimers and advance manually (rejected — adds harness complexity; the 50ms real-time wait is sufficient and self-explanatory)

assumptions.context: Cross-format test — script content as inline strings vs separate fixture files
assumptions.choice: Inline runner-script strings inside the cross-format.test.ts test bodies, written to a per-test mkdtemp directory. Keeps the harness self-contained — each test writes its specific runner script under tempdir, spawns Node against it, then cleans up. Avoids a separate `tests/fixtures/cross-format-runners/` tree that would need its own ESLint exemptions for being non-vitest .cjs/.mjs files.
alternatives_considered: Pre-built runner files at tests/fixtures/cross-format/runner.cjs + runner.mjs (rejected — adds toolchain complexity; the test's intent is clearer when the script content lives next to the assertions that verify its output)
Use a single CommonJS-compatible runner that detects format at runtime (rejected — defeats the purpose; we want to prove the published exports map drives EACH resolver path independently)

assumptions.choice: Construct the error from the CJS bundle and assert `err.name === '<class-name>'` directly. Real cross-bundle instanceof failure requires loading both ESM and CJS bundles in the SAME Node process — an unusual setup that mostly arises through interop with package's that have inconsistent exports. The README documents the recipe; this test verifies the underlying invariant (each error's `name` is its constructor's class name verbatim per NFR-DR-D-007) holds in the published artifact. If a future regression set `err.name` to something else (e.g., the parent `Error` constructor's default `'Error'`), this test fails immediately.
alternatives_considered: Spin up a Node process that imports both bundles and triggers a real cross-bundle instanceof miss (rejected — requires a synthetic project shape that's not how consumers typically land in the cross-format scenario; the err.name invariant is the actual contract per NFR-DR-D-007)
Assert via Symbol.for('instanceof') / Symbol.hasInstance custom check (rejected — over-engineered; the documented contract is err.name)
